A1.justification: Both complete, readable 30-page PDFs describe the same OmniMouse study. Their methods, experiments, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original model- and data-scaling experiments, baseline comparisons, behavioral decoding, and supplementary context analyses, including Figures 5–7 and Tables 1, 2, and S7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their reported outcomes, including the supplementary analyses and SENSORIUM evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same tokenization, architecture, 119 masking configurations, prediction procedures, and weighted Poisson/MSE training objective.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same mouse visual-cortex domains, stimulus types, behavioral variables, prediction tasks, and SENSORIUM benchmarks. The revised aggregate neuron counts do not establish changed population or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains MtM, the Latent Model of Schmidt et al., CEBRA, and POYO+ in the same comparisons. The SENSORIUM comparators, including DwiseNeuro-Σ in Table S7, are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Figure 2B revises the reported training volume from 3.1M to 2.3M neurons and from 5.73M to 4.28M neuron-hours. Session counts, splits, metrics, model configurations, and training budgets remain unchanged. This is a limited revision to reported sample volume; neither PDF establishes data removal or experimental reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix C and Figures S1–S3 retain the same prediction examples, temporal-context and population-context sweeps, and unseen-mask analyses. Table S7 retains the same unimodal and multimodal comparisons.

E5.justification: Table S7 retains the five-model ensemble description, different-random-seed information, and the same uncertainty reporting. No repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Experimental scores and rankings in Tables 1, 2, and S7 are unchanged, as are the scaling curves and supplementary prediction findings. For example, data-matched OmniMouse-5M still reports 0.18 forecasting correlation and 0.59 average behavioral decoding correlation. The data-volume revisions concern sample-size reporting under E3.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations (1)–(4) are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract lowers the stated dataset scale from 3.1 million neurons to over 2.3 million, with corresponding revisions in the introduction and Section 3. The claims about over 150 billion neural tokens, multitask capabilities, competitive performance, and data-limited scaling remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 7 and Appendix C retain the same scaling interpretations, context explanations, and limitations concerning per-neuron parameters, interpretability, and spontaneous behavior. No explanation of the revised dataset totals is added.

D1.justification: Appendices A, B, and E retain the same hyperparameters, hardware, distributed-training procedures, baseline implementation details, acquisition methods, and processing instructions. Code access information is unchanged; the compilation paragraph merely crosses a different page boundary.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning. Reference line wrapping changes without substantive bibliographic additions or removals.

P1.justification: Several appendix references change from 'Sec.' to 'App.', alongside the revised neuron-count wording. The section order, explanatory passages, and overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is re-rendered with altered typography and label spacing while retaining its panels and table structure. Minor page reflow moves the beginning of the compilation paragraph from page 23 to page 22. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v1 consistently used approximately 3.1M neurons in its abstract and Figures 1A and 2B. v2 revises the abstract and Figure 2B toward 2.3M but leaves 3.1M in Figure 1A, introducing an unexplained discrepancy in the dataset scale central to the paper. The underlying scientific findings are retained, so the decline is limited to reporting consistency; the minor cross-reference edits do not resolve it.
